paper_title: Measurement of light-by-light scattering and search for axion-like particles with 2.2 nb$^{-1}$ of Pb+Pb data with the ATLAS detector
suggested_experiment_name: ATLAS Pb+Pb light-by-light scattering (2.2 nb^-1, 5.02 TeV)
coupling_convention: 1/Λ_a in TeV^-1 (inverse axion decay constant), as plotted on the y-axis of Figure 10 (right panel)
notes: Limits extracted from Figure 9 (right panel) showing 95% CL upper limits on ALP coupling 1/Λ_a vs mass m_a. The paper states 'The exclusion limits from this analysis are the strongest so far for the mass range of 6 < m_a < 100 GeV.' Cross-section limits range from 70 nb at 6 GeV to 2 nb at 100 GeV. The coupling values were read from the observed limit curve in Figure 9 (right). Conversion from 1/Λ_a [TeV^-1] to g_agamma [GeV^-1] would require g_agamma ≈ (1/Λ_a) / (4π), but the paper reports limits in 1/Λ_a convention, so those raw values are emitted.
